design_api_stubs.md.approved_by: code-review (AutoMode — documentation corrections: §5.2 path note 3-level fix, §7 health/ready MassTransit auto-check documented)

decision_log.decision: No additional NuGet packages needed at the API project level — all runtime dependencies (Serilog, OTel, JWT Bearer, MassTransit, EF Core, FluentValidation) come via the six shared ProjectReferences transitively.
decision_log.rationale: Avoids version conflicts and duplication. Each shared library already pins the correct package versions. Phase 1 stories add only service-specific packages.
decision_log.alternatives_considered: Adding packages explicitly to each API .csproj — rejected because it creates version duplication risk and makes package governance harder.

decision_log.decision: NT-005 creates only Dockerfiles — it does not modify docker-compose.yml.
decision_log.rationale: The nine API service entries in docker-compose.yml were already fully specified by NT-004. NT-005 creates the files those entries reference (the Dockerfiles). This is the minimal-change approach.
decision_log.alternatives_considered: Having NT-005 add the compose entries too — rejected because NT-004 already owns that file and the entries are already correct.

decision_log.decision: Traverse.AI.Abstractions and Traverse.AI.Providers are NOT referenced from any API stub except AICopilot, and even AICopilot defers this reference to Phase 1.
decision_log.rationale: Avoids pulling OpenAI/Anthropic/AWS SDK NuGet transitive dependencies into 8 services that will never use AI capabilities. Minimal-dependency principle (YAGNI).
decision_log.alternatives_considered: Referencing AI projects from AICopilot.Api in Phase 0 — rejected because the AI projects are not used in Phase 0; the reference adds nothing and inflates the project.

decision_log.decision: No additional NuGet packages at API project level — all runtime deps arrive via 6 shared ProjectReference entries transitively. Explicit duplication rejected (version conflict risk).
decision_log.rationale: Adding packages explicitly to each API .csproj creates version duplication risk and makes package governance harder. Phase 1 stories add service-specific packages.

decision_log.decision: NT-005 creates only Dockerfiles — does not modify docker-compose.yml. Nine service entries were fully specified by NT-004.
decision_log.rationale: Minimal-change approach: NT-004 already owns docker-compose.yml with all nine API service entries. NT-005 creates only the Dockerfile paths referenced by those entries.

decision_log.decision: Traverse.AI.Abstractions and Traverse.AI.Providers not referenced from any Phase 0 API stub — avoids AI SDK transitive deps in 8 services that won't use AI. AICopilot defers to Phase 1.
decision_log.rationale: YAGNI: AI projects not used in Phase 0. Referencing them inflates the project and pulls OpenAI/Anthropic/AWS SDK transitive NuGet deps into services that will never use AI capabilities.

decision_log.decision: audit-docs finding: NT-005 implementation replaces the 9 stub Dockerfiles created by NT-004 with the 4-stage template from design §5.5. NT-004 created 2-stage Dockerfiles (build + runtime) as profile-gated stubs; NT-005 owns the final Dockerfiles per the design doc and AC-3/Gherkin requiring 4 stages. No design doc change needed.
decision_log.rationale: The NT-005 design doc §1 and §5.5 are authoritative for the Dockerfile specification. NT-004 created pre-release stubs to enable docker compose config validation; NT-005 replaces them with production-ready 4-stage images. This is within NT-005's existing scope. The NT-004 stubs also contained a defect (reference to non-existent Directory.Build.props) which is automatically corrected by the replacement.

decision_log.decision: Phase 3 is full replacement of NT-004 Dockerfiles (overwrite, not patch) — stubs have structural defect
decision_log.rationale: NT-004 Dockerfiles contain a Directory.Build.props reference defect. Full replacement with the 4-stage template from NT-005 design doc §5.5 corrects the defect and delivers the required multi-stage build.

decision_log.decision: Phase 4 defers docker build to smoke-test phase; Phase 3 verification is structural (grep-based)
decision_log.rationale: Separating structural verification (grep-based) from runtime smoke-testing (docker build + compose up) allows earlier failure detection and cleaner phase boundaries.

decision_log.decision: Per-project partial builds in Phase 2 for early failure detection
decision_log.rationale: Building each API project individually before full solution build catches errors at the source project level, reducing debug time when build failures occur.

decision_log.decision: docker-compose.yml excluded from NT-005 scope — NT-004 owns it, 9 service entries already exist
decision_log.rationale: Minimal-change principle: docker-compose.yml was fully specified by NT-004. NT-005 creates only the Dockerfile paths those entries reference.

decision_log.decision: No AI lib references in any Phase 0 stub (YAGNI)
decision_log.rationale: AI projects not used in Phase 0. Referencing Traverse.AI.Abstractions/Providers from non-AICopilot stubs inflates projects and pulls unnecessary transitive NuGet dependencies.

decision_log.decision: ProjectReference relative path uses ../../../shared/ (3 levels) not ../../../../shared/ as planned
decision_log.rationale: Services at src/services/<svc>/Traverse.<Svc>.Api/ are 3 levels from src/shared/ — documented in ADR-009

decision_log.decision: Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi 10.0.3 added explicitly — not transitively supplied by shared libs
decision_log.rationale: Package required for OpenAPI endpoint mapping in each API stub. Not included in shared libraries. Added to each API .csproj individually.

decision_log.decision: Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK instruction omitted — docker-compose.yml healthcheck is authoritative
decision_log.rationale: Docker-compose.yml already specifies healthcheck for all services. Duplicate HEALTHCHECK in Dockerfile creates maintenance inconsistency — docker-compose overrides it anyway.
